about: The number the whole chain was missing: how often a filter that has read the document is right. Two filters of the house bench, each against the atlas form it answers, on 300 real JATS articles.
the rule that keeps it from being a mirr: The injection is derived from the form's DATED OBSERVATION and never from the filter's code. form-107 writes the shape observed on 2026-08-08, a review-report DOI built by appending .rNNN; form-120 writes the shape observed on PMC13162546, `X. Shao et al.` against `Xianyun Shao` on page one. Both filters were written before this bench existed. An earlier attempt injected the very character class a filter removes and scored 298/298, which measured the loop and nothing else.
corpus: 300 Europe PMC JATS articles held locally

filter_107.against: form-107, a second DOI on the document
filter_107.the same fault through the textbook read: 298 of 298 returned a DOI without blinking
filter_107.the eleven are a real defect, and it is: They declare the SAME DOI three times. The filter counts DECLARATIONS where it should count DISTINCT VALUES: three identical declarations leave nothing to choose. Measured with the corrected rule on the same 300 documents: 298 right, ZERO wrong silences, and still 298 of 298 abstentions on the damaged ones. The fix costs nothing and is not applied here — the filter belongs to its author.

filter_120.against: form-120, a second spelling of an author in the running head
filter_120.the same fault through the textbook read: 0 of 300 — it reads contrib and never looks at alt-title
filter_120.counter_test_on_clean_documents: 0 false positives. Four documents looked like false triggers and are not: they declare their authors on page one ALREADY abbreviated — `C. G. Bonde`, `L. E. Anselmino` — so the filter recognises an abbreviated spelling and reconciles it to the only candidate, itself. The counter-test assumed page one is always complete, and four documents say otherwise.

reading: p = 0.863 for filter 120, and the shape matters as much as the figure: 86.3 % reconstituted, 13.7 % refused, ZERO wrong. A refusal costs a weight; a wrong answer would poison one.

Both filters answer exactly where the textbook reader is blind — 298 of 298 and 300 of 300. That is the measured version of `a better assembly recovers more`: not more cleverness, a reader that looks where the other does not, plus a filter that refuses where it cannot tell.

from: measures/rival-weights-pgrepair-2026-09-12.json: with a weight of accuracy p, the repairer keeps 130 x p of 130 rivals; with none it lands on a coin at 65
this record: p = 0.863 with 13.7 % abstention and no wrong answer
projection, labelled as such because it.says: a filter measured at 0.863 would take the blind rival arm from 65 of 130 — a coin — to about 121 of 130. It is a projection and not a measurement: the filter was measured on JATS articles and the repairer on an EUR-Lex graph. Running one into the other needs a corpus that is both, and that does not exist yet.
